title: Tension and Release
summary: Build a solo with notes that pull, then let go by landing on the root, 3rd or 5th. Type in a progression and the lesson shows every tense note, where it wants to go and a bar-by-bar plan for the build and the release.
description: Learn how guitar solos build tension and release it on the root, 3rd or 5th. Type a chord progression to see every tense note and exactly where it resolves.
seoTitle: Tension and Release on Guitar: Resolve to the 3rd | Gametape Licks
intro: Tension is a note that pulls. Release is the note it pulls toward. A solo that only plays safe notes never goes anywhere, and a solo that never lands never relaxes. Great jam-band guitar lives between the two. This lesson shows you which notes pull, where each one wants to go and how to plan a build and a landing over any progression you type.

The inspiration is Trey Anastasio of Phish and Rick Mitarotonda of Goose. Both can stretch a phrase until the crowd leans in, then drop onto a chord tone and let everyone breathe. Lesson 1 taught you where the 3rds are. This lesson teaches you when to leave them and how to come back.
